nodes.name: params.rs
nodes.summary: Parses and validates await-tool parameters (handle lists, wait mode, tail-line counts) and resolves job handles against the background registry.

nodes.name: parse_handles
nodes.summary: Parses the one-or-many `handles` parameter (single string or array) into a validated list, enforcing the max-handles-per-call guard.

nodes.name: parse_wait_mode
nodes.summary: Parses the optional `wait_mode` parameter into the `any`/`all` enum, defaulting to `any`.

nodes.name: resolve_job_or_unknown
nodes.summary: Looks up a job handle in the background registry, returning a placeholder 'unknown' snapshot when the handle has no matching job.

nodes.name: response.rs
nodes.summary: Builds the canonical text/meta response payloads for the await tool's wait_for/monitor (aggregated snapshot) and list (table) subcommands.

nodes.name: build_response
nodes.summary: Aggregates one or many HandleSnapshots into the canonical text/meta response body (`[<handle>: <label>] ...` plus tailed output) for wait_for/monitor.

nodes.name: build_list_response
nodes.summary: Renders a list of job snapshots as a table response for the `list` subcommand.

nodes.name: snapshot.rs
nodes.summary: Defines HandleSnapshot and status-resolution helpers that capture a single background job's state at a point in time for rendering by the await tool's response builders.

nodes.name: HandleSnapshot
nodes.summary: Canonical point-in-time representation of one background handle (status, exit code, killed flag, waited time, pattern-match info, output body) shared by the wait_for and monitor subcommands.

nodes.name: resolve_status
nodes.summary: Resolves a raw JobStatus into a display-friendly ResolvedStatus (running/succeeded/failed/killed) plus exit code, unifying shell and subagent job semantics.

nodes.name: to_meta_item
nodes.summary: Converts a HandleSnapshot into the structured meta item shape included in the await tool's machine-readable response.

nodes.name: running_snapshot
nodes.summary: Constructs a HandleSnapshot for a still-running job, including elapsed wait time and any pattern-match info.

nodes.name: terminal_snapshot
nodes.summary: Constructs a HandleSnapshot for a finished (succeeded/failed/killed) job from its terminal status and output body.

nodes.name: external.rs
nodes.summary: Launches shell commands in the user's external OS terminal (Terminal.app, common Linux emulators, or Windows Terminal/PowerShell) instead of the integrated PTY, with per-platform command quoting.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `#[cfg(...)]`-gated platform variants of `launch_for_platform` for macOS, Linux, and Windows rather than runtime branching.

nodes.name: parse
nodes.summary: Parses the optional `terminal_target` string parameter ("integrated"/"external") into a TerminalTarget enum, defaulting to integrated.

nodes.name: launch_for_platform
nodes.summary: Launches the given command in the user's external OS terminal application, with three `#[cfg(...)]`-gated implementations for macOS (osascript/Terminal.app), Linux (common terminal emulators), and Windows (Windows Terminal/PowerShell).
nodes.languageNotes: Three separate cfg-gated definitions of the same function name are merged into a single node here; only one is compiled per target OS.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Defines `ExecTool`, the `run_shell` agent tool that executes commands either as a fast subprocess or, for interactive sessions, via a persistent PTY, including command-confirmation and security-policy gating.
nodes.languageNotes: Large (887-line) tool implementation combining trait-based dependency injection (router, security policy, permission provider) with async command dispatch.

nodes.name: ExecTool
nodes.summary: Tool struct implementing `run_shell`, holding the working directory, PTY resources, security policy, permission provider, cancel flag, and session key needed to execute commands via subprocess or PTY with confirmation gating.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Constructs an ExecTool with a working directory, timeout, and workspace-restriction flag for the subprocess-only (non-PTY) execution path.

nodes.name: new_with_pty
nodes.summary: Constructs an ExecTool wired with PTY session storage and the Tauri app handle, enabling the interactive PTY execution path.

nodes.name: request_command_confirmation_inner
nodes.summary: Core logic for deciding whether a shell command requires explicit user confirmation before running, consulting the security policy and permission provider and handling the force-prompt override.

nodes.name: description
nodes.summary: Returns the human-readable tool description for run_shell surfaced to the LLM.

nodes.name: llm_description
nodes.summary: Builds the full LLM-facing description of run_shell, covering subprocess vs interactive PTY modes and backgrounding/await_output follow-up.

nodes.name: parameters
nodes.summary: Builds the JSON schema for run_shell's command/interactive/timeout/kill_handle parameters.

nodes.name: execute_text
nodes.summary: Main entry point for run_shell: validates the command against the security policy, requests confirmation if needed, then dispatches to the subprocess or PTY execution path and formats the result.

nodes.name: pty.rs
nodes.summary: Manages persistent PTY (pseudo-terminal) sessions shared with the frontend terminal UI, initializing sessions on demand and executing commands within them for interactive use cases (sudo, ssh, password prompts).

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Constructs PtyResources wrapping the shared PTY session map and Tauri app handle.

nodes.name: ensure_pty_initialized
nodes.summary: Ensures a persistent PTY session exists for the agent, spawning and registering one against the given working directory if it doesn't already exist.

nodes.name: execute_via_pty
nodes.summary: Sends a command into a persistent PTY session and waits (bounded by wait_secs) for output, returning immediately with a background handle if the command doesn't complete in time.

nodes.name: registry.rs
nodes.summary: Global in-memory registry tracking backgrounded shell processes and subagent jobs (BackgroundJob) with live broadcast channels, so the await tool can subscribe to output and query status via a unified string handle.
nodes.languageNotes: Central shared-state module with process-tree signal handling that has platform-specific (unix/windows) implementations of terminate_shell_process_tree.

nodes.name: BackgroundJob
nodes.summary: Registry entry tracking one backgrounded shell process or subagent job — its status, output broadcast channel, recent output ring buffer, join handle, and cancel flag — with methods to subscribe, snapshot, and record output.

nodes.name: snapshot
nodes.summary: Captures a point-in-time JobSnapshot (status, recent output) of a BackgroundJob for polling consumers.

nodes.name: register_shell
nodes.summary: Registers a newly-backgrounded shell process (pid, command, log path, session) as a BackgroundJob in the registry.

nodes.name: register_subagent
nodes.summary: Registers a launched background subagent job under a handle scoped to its session.

nodes.name: register_subagent_with_flag
nodes.summary: Registers a background subagent job together with its cancellation flag so it can later be cooperatively cancelled.

nodes.name: broadcast_subagent_job_changed
nodes.summary: Emits a frontend event notifying that a subagent job's status changed, for live UI updates.

nodes.name: mark_exited
nodes.summary: Marks a background job as exited with a terminal status, updating the registry entry and notifying subscribers.

nodes.name: remove
nodes.summary: Removes a job from the registry, replacing it with a tombstone so late status queries still resolve gracefully.

nodes.name: resolve_status_with_tombstone
nodes.summary: Resolves a handle's status, falling back to tombstone records for jobs that have already been removed from the live map.

nodes.name: list_shell_for_session
nodes.summary: Lists all shell background jobs registered for a given session id.

nodes.name: list_jobs
nodes.summary: Lists all background jobs (shell and subagent) registered for a given session id.

nodes.name: claim_subagent_wake_for_session
nodes.summary: Atomically claims the 'wake dispatched' flag for a session's finished subagent jobs so only one wake notification fires per completion.

nodes.name: release_subagent_wake_for_session
nodes.summary: Releases the previously-claimed wake flag for a session's subagent jobs.

nodes.name: list_running_shell_jobs
nodes.summary: Returns all currently-running shell jobs across all sessions, used for process-tree cleanup and diagnostics.

nodes.name: list_running_subagent_jobs
nodes.summary: Returns all currently-running subagent jobs across all sessions.

nodes.name: send_signal_to_process_tree
nodes.summary: Sends a POSIX signal to an entire process tree rooted at the given pid.

nodes.name: terminate_shell_process_tree
nodes.summary: Terminates a shell job's entire process tree, with separate `#[cfg(unix)]`/`#[cfg(windows)]` implementations for signal-based (unix) versus taskkill-based (windows) termination.
nodes.languageNotes: Two cfg-gated definitions (unix and windows) of the same function name are merged into a single node here; only one is compiled per target OS.

nodes.name: kill_shell
nodes.summary: Kills a registered shell job's process tree and marks it as killed in the registry.

nodes.name: kill_subagent
nodes.summary: Cancels a running background subagent job, signaling its cancel flag and waiting for it to wind down before marking it killed.

nodes.name: cancel_subagents_for_session
nodes.summary: Cancels all running background subagent jobs for a given session, e.g. when the session is torn down.

nodes.name: subprocess.rs
nodes.summary: Fast subprocess execution path using `tokio::process::Command` with real-time stdout/stderr streaming, process-group signal handling, backgrounding, and cancellation support.

nodes.name: broadcast_exec_output
nodes.summary: Broadcasts a single `agent:exec_output` streaming event chunk (stdout/stderr) to the frontend.

nodes.name: broadcast_process_started
nodes.summary: Broadcasts an event announcing that a subprocess has started, including its pid, command, and log path.

nodes.name: broadcast_process_exited
nodes.summary: Broadcasts an event announcing that a subprocess exited, including its exit code and whether it was killed.

nodes.name: broadcast_process_backgrounded
nodes.summary: Broadcasts an event announcing that a still-running subprocess was moved to the background (timeout exceeded).

nodes.name: format_command_result
nodes.summary: Formats a subprocess's stdout, stderr, and exit code into the tool-result text shown to the LLM.

nodes.name: signal_process_group
nodes.summary: Sends a signal to an entire process group (not just the leader) so subprocess trees terminate cleanly.

nodes.name: terminate_child_tree
nodes.summary: Terminates a child process and any of its descendants, escalating from graceful signal to force-kill as needed.

nodes.name: configure_git_environment
nodes.summary: Sets environment variables on a spawned command so git subcommands behave non-interactively (no pager, no prompts) under agent control.

nodes.name: finish_cancelled_process
nodes.summary: Cleans up a subprocess that was cancelled mid-flight: kills it, finalizes its log, and clears session bookkeeping.

nodes.name: execute_via_command
nodes.summary: Spawns and drives a subprocess to completion (or timeout/backgrounding), streaming stdout/stderr in real time, honoring the cancel flag, and writing output to the terminal log.

nodes.name: handle_backgrounded
nodes.summary: Takes over a still-running subprocess after the foreground wait window elapses, registering it in the background job registry and continuing to stream its output asynchronously.
